**Does this PR introduce a breaking change?**
No
<!-- If this PR introduces a breaking change, please describe the impact and a migration path for existing applications. -->

**What needs to be documented once your changes are merged?**

Add two options to https://webpack.js.org/configuration/module/#moduleparser

for `json`

- `parse` - Function that executes for a module source string and should return json-compatible data.  Type `((input: string) => any)`, for For example we can use toml parser 

```js
const toml = require("toml");
 
module.exports = [
	{ 
		module: {
			rules: [
				{
					test: /\.toml$/,
					type: "json",
					parser: {
						parse(input) { 
							return toml.parse(input);
						}
					}
				}
			]
		}
	}
];
```
 
- `exportsDepth` - The depth of json dependency flagged as `exportInfo`. In dev mode - 1, in prod - Infinity, Type `number`

issue_context.title: FlagDependencyExportsPlugin is slow with large JSON imports
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please don't delete this template because we'll close your issue -->
<!-- Before creating an issue please make sure you are using the latest version of webpack. -->

# Bug report

<!-- Please ask questions on StackOverflow or the GitHub Discussions. -->
<!-- https://github.com/webpack/webpack/discussions -->
<!-- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/ask?tags=webpack -->
<!-- Issues which contain questions or support requests will be closed. -->

**What is the current behavior?**

Projects importing large JSON files take multiple seconds to build, even incremental builds in watch mode. Most of the time in incremental rebuilds is spent in FlagDependencyExportsPlugin loading values from memory cache, in [`restoreProvided`](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/blob/d9ce3b1f87e63c809d8a19bbd92257d65922e81f/lib/FlagDependencyExportsPlugin.js#L81)

**If the current behavior is a bug, please provide the steps to reproduce.**

<!-- A great way to do this is to provide your configuration via a GitHub repository -->
<!-- The most helpful is a minimal reproduction with instructions on how to reproduce -->
<!-- Repositories with too many files or large `webpack.config.js` files are not suitable -->
<!-- Please only add small code snippets directly into this issue -->
<!-- https://gist.github.com is a good place for longer code snippets -->
<!-- If your issue is caused by a plugin or loader, please create an issue on the loader/plugin repository instead -->

I've created a minimal repro here: https://github.com/albertxing/webpack-json-issue
With a large, deeply nested JSON default import, a lot of time (on my computer, 2-3s on every rebuild) is spent computing and re-hydrating the export tree, even though we only use the default export, and no tree shaking is required.

**What is the expected behavior?**

<!-- "It should work" is not a helpful explanation -->
<!-- Explain exactly how it should behave -->

FlagDependencyExportsPlugin shouldn't take multiple seconds to process large JSON files, especially during incremental rebuilds in watch mode.
I can think of a few options we could explore:
- Skip some of the expensive export tree computations specifically for default imports of JSON modules
- Allow a maximum export depth to be specified in the webpack config for JSON files
  - webpack 4 only computed top-level exports for JSON: https://github.com/webpack/webpack/blob/v4.47.0/lib/JsonParser.js#L20
- Allow disabling FlagDependencyExportsPlugin entirely for JSON modules via config

**Other relevant information:**
webpack version:  5.91.0
Node.js version: v20.12.2
Operating System: macOS
Additional tools:
comments:
> Allow a maximum export depth to be specified in the webpack config for JSON files
> webpack 4 only computed top-level exports for JSON: 
> https://github.com/webpack/webpack/blob/v4.47.0/lib/JsonParser.js#L20

I am fine with it

Do you want to send a PR?
Why do you use `FlagDependencyExportsPlugin` for devevelopment purposes?

You can disable `optimization.providedExports` in development, webpack enabled it by default in development, the only case I encountered where enabling `providedExports` in development mode was effective is `re-exports + cycle reference`, `SideEffectsFlagPlugin` will use provided exports to skip the re-exports module, which avoid the error caused by cycle reference in re-exports module, but in actual usage scenarios, this situation is very rare. (I'm not sure whether there are other reasons for enabling providedExports in development by default)

In your provided reproduce, with `optimization.providedExports = false`, ~2s -> ~70ms for every rebuild
Maybe good place to look how we can speedup it (cache? better logic? etc)

We experimented with disabling `optimization.providedExports`, and while this did make the development build faster, it also silenced errors related to incorrectly named exports. For example, changing a named export while in watch mode would normally show a build error if not all imports were updated with the new name, but after removing the `providedExports` optimization this was no longer the case. I'm not sure if this is a bug or expected behaviour.

At the moment our temporary solution has been to use a slightly updated version of the [old json-loader](https://github.com/webpack-contrib/json-loader) instead of using Webpack's built-in JSON generation, but it'd be great to remove this shim and get a fix in upstream.

I'm happy spending some more time on this writing a max depth PR and potentially looking at performance optimizations when I get a chance!
